bullets.title: META: Muse AI agent drives +10% rally; major product catalyst day
bullets.body: META surged ~10.4% as CEO Tobi Lutke announced an agentic checkout integration (Shop Pay via Muse) across Shopify stores, META launched a 'Petal' petabit-capacity transoceanic subsea cable connecting US-France, and Muse posted 1.8M downloads and 642k DAU in its first 12 days vs ChatGPT's 1.3M/231k at the same stage. Research notes frame Muse as a potential inflection point that could close META's monetization gap with Google in high-intent ad categories (travel, financial services, automotive), with revenue per employee already doubling to $2.9M on flat headcount since early 2023. META also broke above its 200-day MA at the widest margin in 12 months.

bullets.title: AMD: hits $1T market cap for first time; stock +9% on AI CPU demand surge
bullets.body: AMD crossed $1 trillion market cap for the first time, with the stock up ~9% and hitting all-time highs, driven by surging CPU demand from agentic AI workloads (META's Muse launch cited as key catalyst). AMD warrants tied to OpenAI/Meta partnership moved in-the-money. MindWalk deployed OpenFold3 on AMD MI325X GPUs achieving 5x faster inference, adding validation to AMD's AI workload credentials.

bullets.title: INTC: +13-14% on agentic AI CPU thesis; NVIDIA selected Xeon 6 for DGX Rubin
bullets.body: Intel surged ~13-14% as the market priced in the CPU demand boom from agentic AI—inference workloads run at 3-4 GPUs per CPU vs 7-8 for training, and agentic AI could compress that ratio further toward CPUs. NVIDIA selected Intel Xeon 6 as the host CPU for DGX Rubin NVL8, a significant design win. Research from one account titled 'Muse Drives CPU Demand and Price Hikes Expand Upside; Foundry on Track' also turned positive. A high-ranking Intel employee confirmed the CPU shortage is real.

bullets.title: ARM: +14% as agentic AI CPU demand thesis captures semiconductor sector
bullets.body: ARM rallied ~14% alongside INTC and AMD as the market re-rated CPU exposure on agentic AI demand—commentary flagged that agentic AI could push CPU-to-GPU ratios to 6:1 or higher vs prior projections, implying a potentially order-of-magnitude higher CPU demand than modeled. ARM was named by multiple sources as a top AI agent infrastructure beneficiary.

bullets.title: AMZN blocks META's Muse AI agent from retail site; competitive AI agent battle intensifies
bullets.body: Amazon blocked Meta's Muse AI agent from accessing its online shop, per Bloomberg/Reuters, framing a competitive battle in agentic commerce. Analysts note Amazon faces structural risk if shopping agents become the primary commerce entry point—Amazon is unlikely to build a dominant personal AI assistant—while META's Muse is positioned as the commerce funnel. AMZN was also cited as a beneficiary of the CPU demand build via its Graviton data center chips.

bullets.title: CIEN: Evercore upgrades to Outperform; AI optical networking thesis with $25+ EPS target by FY29
bullets.body: Evercore upgraded Credo Technology to Outperform, projecting 30%+ annual sales growth and EPS above $25 by FY2029, citing AI-driven optical networking demand. The optical networking market is expected to expand at 24% CAGR to $52B by FY2029. One contributor noted the dip was a 'good chance to add.'

bullets.title: CRDO: posts 115% YoY growth but sells off; analysts examine margin/valuation disconnect
bullets.body: Credo Technology posted 115% year-over-year revenue growth yet sold off, with at least one analyst breakdown attributing the move to margin and valuation concerns rather than top-line weakness. The stock was also seen recovering intraday (167→181.2) during the broader semiconductor rally.

bullets.title: NVDA: open-source AI leadership thesis emerges; Grok 4.7 built on NVDA compute
bullets.body: NVIDIA's compute advantage for open-source AI models is being cited as a strategic opportunity—NVDA acquired Poolside and invested in Hugging Face, positioning it as an open alternative to OpenAI/Anthropic if the US government backs open-source AI. SpaceX's Grok 4.7 launch was confirmed to run on NVIDIA accelerated computing. However, NVDA's implied vol remains negative for the year and one source maintained caution while the broader GAI infrastructure IV started bottoming.

bullets.title: SHOP: rallies on Shopify-Meta Muse agentic checkout partnership via Shop Pay
bullets.body: Shopify stock moved higher after CEO Tobi Lutke announced a partnership with Meta's Muse for agentic checkout integration via Shop Pay across all Shopify stores. One contributor noted that retailers embracing shopping agents will gain a competitive edge, with SHOP expected to see volume lift as AI agents become the primary commerce entry point.

bullets.title: AXTI: +12.4% on S&P SmallCap 600 inclusion + InP substrate geopolitical angle
bullets.body: AXTI surged 12.4% on its S&P SmallCap 600 inclusion (effective Sept 21 open), driving passive fund demand. Beyond index flows, at least one source suggested AXTI is being used as a geopolitical positioning tool given InP substrates are a key bottleneck for US AI optical infrastructure—control of InP pricing may be relevant in Xi-Trump discussions.

bullets.title: PLTR: Trump filed June 24 PLTR purchase; stock +56% since; $244M Pentagon memo followed
bullets.body: A disclosure surfaced that President Trump filed a Palantir stock purchase on June 24. On August 4, a Pentagon memo directed up to $244M for Palantir. PLTR has risen 56% since the trade date. Palantir exec Chad Wahlquist appeared in a live interview discussing data ownership in AI.

bullets.title: TSLA: Oppenheimer reiterates Perform; AI pivot progressing but Optimus delays likely
bullets.body: Oppenheimer maintained a Perform rating on Tesla, noting progress on the company's AI transformation and Physical AI platform development, but flagging likely delays for Optimus. The firm cited Tesla's vertical integration strategy and semiconductor push as longer-term positives. Tesla was +1.5% in premarket alongside the broader Mag 7 rally.

bullets.title: WBD: Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery merger clears state AG antitrust settlement
bullets.body: Paramount settled antitrust lawsuits with a coalition of state attorneys general, clearing the path for the Warner Bros. Discovery acquisition. Key settlement terms: WBD commits at least $1.5B to domestic film production over 5 years, editorial-independence board for CNN/CBS, $5M/year for 5 years for independent film fund, and an internal compliance monitor overseen by a 5-state committee. Paramount and WBD shares jumped on the news.

bullets.title: LITE/GLW: collaborating on optical die-to-die interconnect demo for AI at ECOC 2026
bullets.body: Lumentum and Corning will jointly demonstrate high-density optical die-to-die interconnect technology using a 1060nm VCSEL platform, D2D interface IP, and multimode fiber targeting CPO/NPO architectures at ECOC 2026 in Málaga. The demonstration positions both companies in the next wave of AI optical connectivity beyond traditional fiber.

bullets.title: MU/semiconductor memory: CXMT G5 DRAM enters mass production; SK Hynix flags survival pressure
bullets.body: China's CXMT launched its G5 DRAM platform into mass production with 50% higher die-per-wafer density using SAQP at 11.95nm half-pitch, approaching world-leading specifications and increasing competitive pressure on MU and SK Hynix. A SK Hynix packaging executive separately stated 'there isn't much time left to survive on memory,' flagging urgency around the HBM transition.

bullets.title: AAPL: Tim Cook legacy/Siri critique; $12,300 Mac launched; iPhone 18 Pro Max detail
bullets.body: Bloomberg's Mark Gurman discussed Siri's limitations and Tim Cook's legacy, noting John Ternus as incoming CEO. Apple launched a $12,300 computer with mixed reviewer reception. The iPhone 18 Pro Max reportedly removes a 20Wh firmware lock upon user activation. One source argued Apple has a trust/privacy advantage in consumer agents but market skeptics question whether privacy drives actual behavior.

bullets.title: NET/TWLO: named as top AI agent infrastructure plays alongside META
bullets.body: Cloudflare (NET) and Twilio (TWLO) were cited alongside META as the top 3 'AI Agent' names ripping on the day, per one research account tracking agentic commerce positioning. No specific fundamental catalysts were detailed for NET or TWLO beyond their infrastructure roles in agent communication and task-routing.

bullets.title: NBIS/CRWV: GPU pricing resilience — Nebius raised rates 17-21% despite claims of falling prices
bullets.body: One source argued Nebius's financing model is more sustainable than CoreWeave's, pointing to Nebius raising GPU cloud rates 17-21% despite persistent market narrative about falling GPU pricing. Oracle also raised pricing for 4+ year equipment contracts, validating durable pricing power in the neocloud segment.

bullets.title: GOOGL: purchase-intent signal gap vs META narrowing via Muse; Gemini 4 still on TPU
bullets.body: Multiple research threads flagged that META's Muse could close a 7.5-point travel and 6-point financial-services ad revenue gap vs Google by capturing purchase-intent signals even from incomplete checkout flows. Separately, a clarification emerged that Gemini 4 was NOT trained on NVIDIA GPUs—Google's stack remains on JAX/XLA/Pathways compiled to TPU topology, dispelling a rumor that represented a potential NVDA demand pull-forward.

bullets.title: TSM: mentioned in CPU demand bull thesis alongside INTC, AMD, ARM as key beneficiary
bullets.body: Taiwan Semiconductor was grouped with INTC, AMD, and ARM in the agentic AI CPU demand thesis, with sources noting all four showed strength at the open. No TSM-specific fundamental catalyst was cited beyond the sector tailwind from the META Muse-driven CPU demand thesis.
